structured_output.world_model:
So far there is one data point. E000 is the template demo: 64 images and 3 SGD steps. It scored 0.012 accuracy, which is chance for 100 classes, in 0.14 s. Nothing about the real recipe has been measured yet, so this model runs on priors from airbench and CIFAR-100 speedrun experience.

How the time arises: time ≈ prepare (H2D copy of 150 MB uint8, normalisation, whitening eig on patches, about 0.1-0.3 s) + epochs × (time per step × steps per epoch) + leaked warm-up (cuDNN autotune and allocator growth at the first real step). On an A100 with eager fp16 and channels_last, an airbench96-width net (128/384/576, about 3× the FLOPs of airbench94) should take about 1.1-1.4 s per epoch at batch 1024. That puts 9 eager epochs at about 10-13 s. The work is GPU-bound once data lives on the GPU, so the 4-CPU pin barely matters. Launch overhead at batch 1024 is small relative to the conv FLOPs. torch.compile helps mainly by fusing BN-GELU elementwise ops and saving memory bandwidth, worth about 15-25%. CUDA graphs and dropping the ragged batch are worth only a few percent.

How the accuracy arises: CIFAR-100 at 9 epochs is sample-starved. Each class has 500 images, so the triangular LR, patch-whitening (fast early feature learning), LS 0.3 (calibration under 100 classes) and alternating flip (2× effective, deterministic data diversity) carry most of the accuracy. Without TTA, I expect about 0.73-0.76 at 9 epochs, so the 0.753 bar sits right at the edge. Around 9-10 epochs, accuracy likely rises about 0.5-0.8 pp per extra epoch. Changes that reduce information per epoch should cost accuracy roughly in proportion to the information lost. Progressive resizing does this, and so does a larger batch (fewer updates). Changes that only remove overhead (compile, fused SGD) leave accuracy unchanged up to fp16 nondeterminism.

Noise: I expect per-seed accuracy std of about 0.2-0.4 pp, so the std of the 3-seed mean is about 0.15-0.25 pp. Run-to-run time drift should be under 2%. Effects of 0.2 pp (EMA, LS) are therefore barely resolvable with one run.

Unsure about:
(a) whether the port has bugs; a first ports often has whitening or LR-scaling bugs that cost several pp;
(b) the real eager time per epoch on SXM4;
(c) whether 9 epochs without TTA reaches 0.753 at all, or needs about 10-12 epochs.

forecasts.reason: An eager airbench96-width net is about 1.2 s per epoch, so the run likely exceeds 9.5 s, and without TTA 9 epochs sits at or just below the 0.753 bar.
The port probably lacks a 0.3 pp margin, so this runs 9→10 epochs rather than the 8.5↔9 slope the hypothesis asks about; I expect about +0.6 pp for +10% time.
Inductor fuses the BN-GELU memory-bound ops and foreach SGD cuts launches, a 15-25% speedup with the same math.
The expected gain is about +0.2-0.4 pp, the same size as the std of the 3-seed mean, and the time cost is small.
With GPU-bound deterministic-shape work, time should drift under 2% and per-seed std should land around 0.2-0.35 pp.
If the ragged shape was already warmed up, dropping it saves only about 0.1-0.2 s, below the 0.3 s threshold.
Batch 2000 halves the number of updates at a fixed epoch count. Untuned Muon on this net likely fails to recover that, and eager Newton-Schulz adds overhead.
The schedule cuts about 20% of FLOPs, but crop and interpolation lose information per epoch and the BN/resolution shift costs about 0.5-1 pp, far above the 0.2 pp budget.

cruxes: What 3-seed accuracy does the 9-epoch port reach without TTA: is it above 0.753, or does it need 10-12 epochs?
What is the measured eager time per epoch of the 128/384/576 net on the A100-SXM4, and how much of it does torch.compile remove?
How much fixed overhead (prepare, first-step cuDNN autotune, allocator growth) sits inside the timed region?
